name: cpp-netlib
listed_description: A collection of open-source libraries for high level network programming.
reason: No numeric comparison against a named baseline. README.rst, libs/network/doc and libs/network/benchmarks/README.rst (a two-line stub about collecting statistics) carry no benchmark numbers. The only figure found is a 2010 mailing-list report of about 4700 requests/s for the static-server example with Apache ab on a dual-core Core 2, with no baseline.

name: cpr
listed_description: A modern C++ HTTP requests library with a simple but powerful interface. Modeled after the Python Requests module.
reason: No numbers. The repo (now libcpr/cpr) is a libcurl wrapper aimed at usability; README has no benchmark or speed claim and the tree has no benchmark directory. WebSearch found no overhead-versus-libcurl measurement.

name: czmq
reason: No numeric comparison against a named baseline. README has only absolute notes (zhash about 50K inserts/s and 2.5M lookups/s on a 1.6 GHz CPU; zhash and zhashx 3-4x faster than the draft ztrie matcher, an internal comparison). Same project as the CZMQ entry.

name: CZMQ
reason: Same repo as czmq (zeromq/czmq). No benchmark against a named baseline; README states only internal container notes (zhash 50K inserts/s, 2.5M lookups/s on a 1.6 GHz CPU) and no messaging throughput or latency numbers.

name: easyhttpcpp
listed_description: A cross-platform HTTP client library providing a caching facility from Sony.
reason: Directional claim only: README says 'focus on usability and speed' and 'connection pooling to reduce latency' with no numbers; the wiki (Home, Build options, Recipes and others) has no benchmark or comparison against Poco, cpprestsdk or libcurl.

name: eCAL
listed_description: Pub/sub, client/server, C++/Python/C#, various message protocols
reason: No named baseline. Repo moved to eclipse-ecal/ecal. README claims 1-20 GB/s and doc/rst/advanced/performance.rst gives absolute 1:1 shared-memory latencies (about 3 us zero-copy and 8 us at 1 kB on Ubuntu 22, HP ZBook 15 G5) with no comparison against ROS 2, DDS, ZeroMQ or iceoryx. bencher.dev is regression tracking only. WebSearch found no third-party eCAL comparison.
